symptom: `SHOW VERSION` prints `MPR Format: v2` for an MPR v1 project (single .mpr, no mprcontents/); `STATUS` and the session log's `mpr_format` (shipped by `diag --bundle`) say 2 as well, while `diff-local`, `diag --check-units` and `fix hashes` on the same project correctly treat it as v1
cause: Two answers to one question. The reader decides v1/v2 from disk (mprcontents/ beside the .mpr, reconciled by the Unit.Contents column) and reads units with that; `ProjectVersion.FormatVersion` came separately from `version.DetectFromDB`, which reads `_MetaData._FormatVersion` and, when the column is missing, assumed 'a newer schema (11.6.2+), so 2'. The column is in fact missing because the schema is v1: absent in a 9.24.30 and an 11.13.0 v1 project, present and 2 in 11.6.6/11.13.0/11.14.0 v2 ones
file: `modelsdk/mpr/version/version.go` (`DetectFromDB` no longer sets FormatVersion), `modelsdk/mpr/reader.go` (`reportDetectedFormat`, called in `OpenWithOptions` after the reconciliation and in `OpenWithDB`)
insight: Before trusting a field that reports a fact, find the code that *acts* on the fact and check the two agree: every consumer that branches on the format (`diff-local` guard, harvest, check-units, fix hashes) used `Reader.Version()`, and only the printers used the metadata copy, so the defect was invisible to anything but a human reading the output. The comment justifying the default ('Mendix 11.6.2+') was a guess written as a measurement; one `pragma table_info(_MetaData)` on a v1 file refutes it. Stamp after the Unit.Contents reconciliation, not before it: a v2-schema .mpr copied away from its folder is v1 by the folder test and v2 after reconciliation, and `TestProjectVersionReportsTheDetectedStorageFormat` has a case that fails if the order is swapped. The v2 project is the control: it printed v2 before the fix too (ako/mxcli#1553, upstream mendixlabs/mxcli#1621)
